title: Mobile salon setup, hygiene and tool sterilisation
audience: Mobile hairdressers and barbers who set up a temporary work station at a client's home, a venue or a vehicle
learningOutcomes: Set up a mobile work station that has hand-washing, a treatment area, a sharps container and a wastewater plan
Clean, disinfect and store tools between clients using the method the cited guideline describes
Identify which registration or notification rule applies in your state or territory before the first visit
referencesAtStart: Official references for this lesson: Victorian Department of Health, Information for registered premises and environmental health officers (updated 22 May 2026); WA Health, Guideline for the hairdressing industry (last reviewed February 2024); NSW Health, Skin penetration (current as at 10 August 2023); NT Government, Register a hairdressing, beauty therapy or body art business (no date shown); Queensland Health, Personal appearance services legislation (no date shown); ACT Government, Skin penetration procedures (no date shown).

instruction.heading: Why set-up and hygiene come first
instruction.body: A mobile hairdresser has no salon fit-out to rely on. Every visit starts with an empty room, a borrowed sink or a van, and a client who expects the same standard as a salon. The set-up is therefore the first control you apply to every job. Hair services involve cutting, shaving with blades, and chemicals applied to the scalp and skin. A poorly set-up station can spread infection between clients and can leave chemical residue, sharps and wastewater in a client's home. This lesson teaches the set-up routine, the cleaning and disinfection routine, and the registration questions you must settle for your own state or territory. The content is drawn from research notes.

instruction.heading: Mobile facilities in the WA guideline (confirmed for Western Australia only)
instruction.body: The Western Australian Chief Health Officer guideline for the hairdressing industry, issued under the Public Health Act 2016 and last reviewed in February 2024, has a section for mobile operators (section 13.1). The guideline says mobile operators must have hand-washing facilities that are easily accessible, with warm water, soap and disposable towels, and that hands are cleaned both before and after every client. It requires equipment to be cleaned after each client, a container for sharps, and wastewater sent to the sewer instead of the stormwater system. It also says that an unsuitable treatment area, such as a kitchen, must not be used for hairdressing procedures. These are confirmed requirements for Western Australia. Your set-up checklist should record which source you used. Do not assume that a van, a bathroom or a kitchen sink meets the requirement until you have checked it against the source for your location.

instruction.heading: Cleaning, disinfection and blood-contaminated tools
instruction.body: The title of this lesson uses the word sterilisation. The WA guideline does not use that word. Where equipment is contaminated with blood, the guideline suggests cleaning it first and then placing it in a 70 per cent alcohol solution or a disinfectant of hospital grade. The routine is: remove visible hair and debris, clean with detergent, rinse, then disinfect for the time the product label states. The guideline requires dye mixing bowls to be cleaned after each use, and food should not be prepared in the space where dyes are mixed, and drinks are to be kept away from hairdressing supplies. For blood or body-fluid spills, the guideline allows bleach as a disinfectant for hard-to-clean areas after a detergent clean, and it advises against using chemical disinfectants for everyday cleaning. Every product you make up should carry its name, the date it was made up, and its dilution; that is a business rule in this course. Keep blood-contaminated tools separate from clean tools until they have been cleaned and disinfected.

instruction.heading: Registration and notification: where this lesson stops
instruction.body: This lesson does not register you, and completing it does not give any authority to operate. The rules differ by state and council. In Victoria, the Department of Health lists hairdressing among services that must register under the Public Health and Wellbeing Act 2008 (page updated 22 May 2026). The same page lists mobile hairdressers as exempt from registration, but the exemption stops short of the principal place of business. In the Northern Territory, a business that receives payment for hairdressing must register, and the NT page gives a fee of $91 to register or renew for hairdressing (no date shown). In Queensland, hairdressing is not a higher-risk personal appearance service and needs no licence, but the business must still follow the infection control guidelines for personal appearance services (no date shown). In the ACT, hairdressing needs no infection control licence but must still follow the 2005 infection control Code of Practice for office practices and other community-based services (no date shown). In Western Australia, a home-based operator must contact the local government authority before operating (guideline section 13.2). Check your own state and council before your first client visit.

procedure: Confirm the registration, notification or council position for the state or territory and the council where you will work, and record the source and date checked
Set up a dedicated treatment area at the client's location that is clear of food preparation and out of the path of other people
Confirm that hand-washing facilities with warm water, soap and disposable towels are available, or that you have brought a compliant substitute your state accepts
Place a sharps container within reach and a plan for disposing of used blades and waste
Plan wastewater disposal so that it goes to sewer and never to stormwater
Clean and disinfect each tool between clients, using the product label time, and store clean tools apart from used tools
Label every made-up product with its name, date and dilution, and record the set-up checklist on the job record

workedExamples.situation: A mobile barber in Perth is booked at a client's home. The only sink is in the kitchen, and the barber plans to rinse clippers there and to tip rinse water down the outdoor drain near the back door.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which parts of this plan can go ahead, and which must be checked first?
workedExamples.reasoning: The WA guideline wants holding tanks for wastewater emptied into the sewer rather than stormwater, so an outdoor drain that leads to stormwater is not acceptable unless the connection is confirmed. The guideline also says a kitchen is an example of an inappropriate treatment area for mobile hairdressing procedures, so rinsing clippers in the kitchen should not go ahead without a check of the area. The guideline's home-based operator rule (section 13.2) covers an operator working from their own home. The barber should confirm the drain connection, bring a labelled container for used rinse water if needed, and check the council position before the visit. The kitchen can be used only if it meets the requirements.

workedExamples.situation: A stylist in Victoria finishes a colour service at a client's house. The mixing bowl still has residue, and the stylist plans to leave it in the van for the next day.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should happen to the bowl, and what should be recorded?
workedExamples.reasoning: WA Health's guideline says dye mixing bowls must be cleaned after each use. That guideline applies in Western Australia. The bowl should be cleaned before it leaves the client's home. The stylist should record that the bowl was cleaned, and should check the product's label and date. Residue should not be left in an unlabelled container in the van.

equipmentAndPpe: Portable hand-washing set-up with warm water, soap and disposable towels
Sharps container with a lid, kept upright and within reach
Detergent, rinse water and a disinfectant that is listed on the product label with a contact time
Labelled containers for made-up products, including name, date and dilution
Gloves suitable for the products in use, changed between clients
Waterproof sheet or mat for the treatment area
Wastewater container if the local drain is not an approved sewer connection

commonErrors.error: Treating a mobile visit as if it were a salon with a fixed sink, drainage and storage.
commonErrors.prevention: Complete the set-up checklist before the first service, and record any gap, such as a missing sharps container, before the client sits down.

commonErrors.error: Tipping rinse water into a stormwater drain outside the client's home.
Describing tools as sterilised when the guideline describes cleaning and disinfection.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the words cleaned and disinfected in client records and signage, and follow the product label contact time. Do not claim sterilisation until the team has confirmed the wording.

commonErrors.error: Assuming a registration exemption covers every visit.
commonErrors.prevention: Read the exemption's conditions, including the principal place of business exception on the Department of Health page, and check the Act and council before relying on it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: In Victoria, hairdressing is listed as a service that must register under the Public Health and Wellbeing Act 2008 (page updated 22 May 2026). Mobile hairdressers are listed as exempt but the exemption stops short of the principal place of business.
In the Northern Territory, a business that receives payment for hairdressing must register, and the NT page gives a fee of $91 to register or renew (no date shown).
In New South Wales, operators working from their own vehicle or a temporary structure has to inform the local council.
In Western Australia, home-based operators must contact their local government before operating (guideline section 13.2). This lesson does not confirm any council approval.
The WA guideline requires a sharps container, cleaning of equipment after each client, and wastewater to the sewer.
The WA guideline suggests placing blood-contaminated equipment in a 70 per cent alcohol solution or a disinfectant of hospital grade. This is a WA guideline position.

qualityStandard: The set-up checklist is completed and signed before the first service of every visit
Every tool is cleaned and disinfected between clients, and the method and contact time are recorded
All made-up products carry a name, date and dilution label
Any gap in facilities is recorded with the action taken before the service continues
documentationEvidence: Set-up checklist for each visit, with the time completed
Registration or notification confirmation for the state and council, with the source and date
Disinfectant product name, label contact time and dilution used
Sharps container and waste disposal record
summary: A mobile station needs its own hygiene plan because it is not a salon
The WA guideline sets confirmed mobile requirements for Western Australia.
Clean, then disinfect; use the word sterilisation only after the team confirms it
Completing this lesson does not register you or authorise any service. Check your state and council first

knowledgeChecks.question: Under the Western Australian hairdressing guideline, where must a mobile operator's wastewater be discharged?
options: To the stormwater drain, if the van has no sewer
Into any outdoor drain at the client's address
Into the sewer, keeping it out of stormwater

knowledgeChecks.question: A blood-contaminated tool has been cleaned. Which step does the WA guideline describe next?
options: Placing it in a 70 per cent alcohol solution or a disinfectant of hospital grade
Wiping with a damp cloth and returning the tool straight back into the kit
Storage in the client's bathroom until the next visit, where it stays out of the way

knowledgeChecks.question: A Victorian mobile hairdresser reads the Department of Health's registration list. Which statement matches that page?
options: Mobile hairdressers are exempt from registration everywhere, with no conditions attached to the exemption and no need to check the Act or regulations
Mobile hairdressers are listed as exempt but the exemption stops short of the principal place of business, and the Act should be checked for the visit
Mobile hairdressers must register at every client's home visit, and the register must be kept in the van at all times for the inspector
